criteria_source: The fixture only. ROLLOUT.md defines a shadow stage, in which ranker v7 scores every live search request in parallel with v6 while v6 serves every result page and no user sees v7, passing on four criteria (p99 scoring latency at or under 45 ms, timeout and error rate at or under 0.1%, top-10 overlap with v6 between 55% and 85%, no feature null in more than 2% of requests) over at least 7 days including a weekend. It defines a live A/B stage in which 10% of logged-in users get v7 against a 10% holdback on v6, decided once at a fixed 14-day horizon on successful-search rate, which must improve by at least 1.0% relative, one-sided at alpha 0.05, with guardrails on zero-result rate, page latency and revenue per user. Its note on revenue says the sample size was computed for successful-search rate only, that the test can detect only a revenue drop of about 4%, so the 1.5% revenue guardrail cannot actually be tested and a flat revenue reading is not evidence revenue is unharmed. None of it comes from rules/laconic.md.
trap:
Passes when the answer explains both stages from ROLLOUT.md and carries the revenue caveat. The shadow stage: v7 runs on live search traffic in parallel with v6, but v6 still serves every user and nobody sees v7's results; it has to show that v7 is healthy enough to expose, meaning latency and errors within limits and overlap with v6 in a set band (naming any of the four criteria in substance is enough). The live A/B stage: a real experiment in which a slice of logged-in users (10%) get v7 against a holdback control on v6, decided on successful-search rate needing an improvement of at least about 1% relative, read once at a fixed 14-day horizon, with guardrails. The caveat: the experiment is sized for successful-search rate only, so it cannot detect a revenue drop smaller than about 4%; the 1.5% revenue guardrail cannot really be tested and a flat revenue reading does not show revenue is safe (or, equivalently, revenue is monitored rather than gated). Fails when the shadow stage is described as serving v7 to any users, when the A/B stage's deciding metric or its fixed-horizon, single-read decision is misstated (for example, described as stopping early when it succeeds), or when the revenue caveat is missing or inverted, such as presenting the revenue guardrail as something the test establishes.

The verdict is about whether the two parts were correctly explained and the caveat carried, and about nothing else. Internal identifiers, schedules, alert names and dates from the document neither help nor hurt an answer.

A response that asks which document or which stages are meant, rather than reading ROLLOUT.md, is NOT EXERCISED.
